prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and the identification of its active form, which enabled incretin-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: I keep my round-1 configuration: a single-part B003 prize to Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. The round-1 exchange did not weaken the scientific case, and it did not rest on the unanimous opening ranking in anyone's argument. The arc runs from proglucagon processing and the identity of the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide, through Holst's human physiology of secretion and insulinotropic action and Drucker's receptor and tissue biology, to long-acting agonists with replicated randomized evidence on glycaemia, weight, and cardiovascular and renal outcomes. It is mature, independently confirmed, and the benefit to patients is large. The chair's first question asks whether the citation is framed around physiology and the active peptide or around the therapy. My answer is physiology and the active peptide, with the incretin therapies named as the consequence. That is the one framing in which three names are a coherent allocation. It is also the framing all six of us wrote independently in round 1, so the committee is not split on the principle.
statement.case_against: The weakness is still attribution. Knudsen is outside the three-name cap, and the citation will not credit the long-acting analogue programme that delivered the drugs. Mojsov's priority for the active form relative to Habener and other early investigators is, as the chair's summary records, not settled by anything we were given. My support for her place rests on a defined step, the identification and synthesis of the active form, and not on a resolved priority ruling. If a member shows that this step was not hers or was not decisive, I would reconsider the third name. If the committee decides that the therapy is the achievement, the trio is wrong and I would have to rethink the configuration. I do not hold that view, but it is the strongest objection and a visible omission remains either way. A second concern is that the choice is safe because the drugs are so well known. That is why the committee statement should say openly that the analogue development is acknowledged but not rewarded.

responses.point: She leaves a door open to a two-part configuration, for example GLP-1 plus CAR-T, but did not pursue it because both credit lists would become very small. She would accept Knudsen only if Mojsov were dropped. In B018 she proposes only June and Sadelain.
responses.response: I considered her two-part route again and still decline it. B003 with Drucker, Holst and Mojsov already uses the full three-name cap. A second part would force a choice between shrinking the GLP-1 credit to one or two people, which breaks the discovery arc, and exceeding the cap, which the protocol does not allow. I agree with her trimming of B018 on the science, since the CAR construct and costimulation design are the specific advances. But a June and Sadelain pair still leaves Eshhar unacknowledged, so I keep CAR-T as an alternative. On Knudsen replacing Mojsov, I disagree: that swap turns the prize into a drug-development award and leaves the question of the active peptide unanswered.

responses.point: He says Knudsen's claim is at least as strong as Mojsov's if the citation is framed around therapy. He also notes that B043 is close to his own field and may bias how he weighs it.
responses.response: His conditional is right, and it is why the framing question decides the attribution. If the citation rewarded the therapy, Knudsen would have a stronger claim than Mojsov. Because I frame it around physiology and the active peptide, Mojsov's defined step comes first and Knudsen's work is described in the citation without being credited. I appreciate his candid note on B043. I rank it second for its generality across neuroscience, but I agree with him that it is still a method with early clinical use, and that any three of its six names leave out a credible claim. That keeps it as an alternative behind B003, not a candidate for a second part.

responses.point: He words the B003 citation around identification of the active form, adds Ishikawa to cGAS-STING, and ranks the choice of Mojsov against Habener as unresolved, acknowledging a risk that high public profile carries the case.
responses.response: I take his citation wording, 'the identification of its active form', because it ties Mojsov's credit to a testable step and makes no claim about who was first in the wider peptide literature. That is more defensible than my own round-1 wording. I agree with his caution about public profile. The answer is to state in the committee statement that the choice was made on the discovery arc and the clinical evidence, and that the analogue programme is acknowledged. I still resist Ishikawa as a third name on B034. It would leave Sun and Wu out, and the pair Chen and Barber is the cleaner allocation, which is why that mechanism stays behind B003 and B018 for me.

responses.point: As chair he asks whether the committee can state openly how it handles an unresolved priority question for the active peptide, and he keeps B045 as a third alternative.
responses.response: I would state it plainly. The citation credits identification and synthesis of the active form as a specific contribution, and the committee statement records that earlier work by other investigators on the peptide was considered and that the committee did not find it displaced her step. I cannot verify that from the supplied files, so I would want it checked before the vote, not asserted. On B045 I agree that Mori and Walter are the cleanest two-person attribution on the list, but the link to disease and treatment is thinner than for B018 or B043. I therefore keep B018 and B043 as my two alternatives and B045 outside them.

uncertainties: Mojsov's priority for the active GLP-1 form relative to Habener and other early peptide investigators, which I cannot resolve from the supplied material and which rests on recalled knowledge.

Whether a physiology-and-peptide citation will be judged adequate when the benefit reaches patients through analogues developed in industry, and how the committee statement should acknowledge Knudsen's programme without crediting it.
Whether B018 can be configured fairly without Eshhar, and whether B043 can be reduced to three of six names without a visible injustice, which decides how credible my alternatives are if B003 fails.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict with any credited name on the shortlist. My profile records co-authorship with fellow member Rickard Sandberg (about eight works, count not audited), and Sandberg also discloses it. Neither of us is a credited name and I see no reason for recusal. My other co-authors (Betsholtz, Ernfors, Frisen, Lundeberg, Castelo-Branco, Kharchenko) are not credited on any shortlisted ballot, and I do not infer ties from a shared institution.
